description.en: The 90/90 stretch is a seated hip mobility exercise where both legs are positioned on the floor at 90-degree angles — the front leg in external rotation and the back leg in internal rotation. It effectively stretches both hip rotational directions simultaneously and is one of the best drills for improving overall hip mobility.

en: Sit on the floor. Bend your right knee to 90 degrees in front of you with the outside of your right leg on the floor (external rotation).
Bend your left knee to 90 degrees behind you with the inside of your left leg on the floor (internal rotation).
Both shins should be roughly perpendicular to each other, forming a pinwheel shape.
Sit up tall. Square your torso forward over your right shin.
For a deeper stretch, lean forward over your right shin, keeping your back flat.
Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply.
To switch sides, lift your knees and rotate both legs so the positions reverse.
Perform 2 to 3 holds per side. Use a pillow under your hip if the position is uncomfortable.
Stretches both hip internal and external rotation simultaneously
One of the most effective hip mobility drills
Improves squat depth and hip-hinge flexibility
Helps prevent hip and knee issues
No equipment needed
Used by physical therapists and mobility coaches

musclesWorked: Piriformis and deep hip rotators (front leg, external rotation)

description.en: The assault run is a high-intensity sprint-based conditioning drill. It can be performed as straight sprints, shuttle runs, or interval sprints at near-maximum effort. The goal is to build cardiovascular capacity, speed, and leg power through short, intense bursts of running with recovery periods.

en: Choose a flat, clear surface of at least 20 to 50 meters.
Warm up thoroughly with 5 minutes of jogging and dynamic stretching.
Sprint at 85 to 95 percent of maximum effort for the designated distance or time (typically 10 to 30 seconds).
Walk or jog back to the start for recovery. Rest until your heart rate drops to a manageable level.
Repeat for the desired number of sprints (typically 6 to 12 per session).
Focus on proper sprint mechanics — drive your knees, pump your arms, stay on the balls of your feet.
Do not start with maximum effort on the first rep — build up across the first 2 to 3 sprints.
Cool down with 5 minutes of easy jogging and stretching.
Builds cardiovascular capacity rapidly
Develops speed and leg power
Burns calories at a high rate during and after exercise
Time-efficient conditioning — sessions can be 10 to 20 minutes
Carries over to all athletic performance
No equipment needed — works anywhere with space

description.en: The band hammer curl is a bicep and forearm exercise performed by standing on a resistance band and curling with a neutral (hammer) grip. The band provides increasing tension at the top of the curl, heavily loading the brachialis and brachioradialis. It is an effective at-home arm exercise.

en: Stand on the center of a resistance band with feet hip-width apart.
Grip both ends of the band at your sides with a neutral grip (palms facing your body).
Pin your elbows to your sides. Brace your core. Stand tall.
Curl both hands up by bending at the elbows. Keep the neutral grip throughout.
Continue until your hands reach shoulder height. Squeeze hard at the top.
Lower under control over two seconds.
The band tension is highest at the top — focus on squeezing through the hardest part.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Targets the brachialis and forearms with increasing tension
Highly portable — needs only a band
Effective at-home arm exercise
Easy to scale by changing band thickness
Neutral grip is easy on the wrists
Useful when no dumbbells are available

description.en: The band kickback is a glute isolation exercise where you loop a resistance band around your ankles and kick one leg straight back against the band tension. It targets the gluteus maximus directly with constant tension throughout the movement.

en: Loop a mini band around both ankles. Stand tall, holding a wall or chair for balance.
Shift your weight to your left leg.
Keeping your right leg straight, kick it straight back behind you against the band tension.
Squeeze your right glute hard at the top of the kick.
Do not arch your lower back — the movement comes from your hip, not your spine.
Return your right leg to the start under control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
Aim for 12 to 20 reps per side. Use a thicker band for more resistance.
Directly isolates the gluteus maximus
Constant band tension throughout
Highly portable
Easy to scale by band thickness
Useful for glute activation before squats
Joint-friendly

description.en: The band kneeling rear kick is a quadruped glute builder where a resistance band is looped around the back of one foot. The lifter kicks the leg back to drive against the band tension. The constant band resistance trains the glute hard.

en: Loop a band around a sturdy anchor at floor level.
Get into a quadruped position with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Loop the other end of the band around the back of one foot.
Keep the foot flexed to hold the band in place.
Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Kick the leg straight back against the band tension.
Squeeze the glute hard at the top of the kick.
Lower with control. Complete reps and switch sides.
Loaded glute builder
Constant band tension
No machine needed
Easy to scale
Strong unilateral glute work
Useful at-home option

description.en: The band low alternate chest press is performed with the band anchored low behind you while pressing one handle at a time upward and across the body. The upward press angle targets the lower chest. Alternating arms allows you to focus on each side and improves stability.

en: Anchor a resistance band low behind you.
Stand facing away from the anchor with a handle in each hand.
Hold the handles at your sides at chest level.
Step forward to add tension to the band.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Press one handle up and across your body to chest height in front.
Squeeze the chest at the end of the press.
Return slowly and alternate sides.
Targets the lower chest
Alternating pattern builds stability
No bench required
Easy to set up at home
Builds chest and front delt strength

description.en: The bar band side bend press combines a side bend with an overhead press using a barbell paired with bands. The side bend hits the obliques while the press loads the shoulders, all with accommodating resistance.

en: Loop a resistance band around the bar and anchor both ends.
Stand tall holding the bar at the shoulder rack position.
Brace the core and feet shoulder width apart.
Bend laterally to one side, dropping the elbow toward the hip.
Reverse and stand back tall, then press the bar up overhead.
Lock out the elbows at the top of the press.
Lower the bar back to the rack and bend to the opposite side.
Continue alternating side bends with presses for all reps.
Hits the obliques through the side bend.
Builds shoulder strength with banded press.
Trains anti lateral flexion control.
Develops core stability under overhead load.
Combines two movements for time efficiency.
Bands accommodate the strength curve.

description.en: The barbell behind the back deadlift, also known as the old-school hack squat lift, is performed with the barbell held behind your legs at hip level. Lifting the bar from behind shifts the emphasis from the posterior chain to the quads and traps. It is a classic strongman and bodybuilding lift.

en: Stand with the barbell on the floor directly behind your heels.
Bend at the hips and knees and reach behind you to grip the bar with palms facing back.
Use a shoulder-width grip just outside your hips.
Pull your shoulders back and engage your lats.
Brace your core and lift your chest.
Drive through your heels to stand up, lifting the bar along the back of your legs.
Lock out at the top with the bar against the back of your thighs.
Lower the bar back to the floor by hinging at the hips and bending the knees.
Targets quads and traps differently than conventional deadlift
Old-school strongman variation
Strong grip and forearm work from the unusual position
Reduces lower back stress compared to floor pulls
Builds upper trap mass
Useful variation for breaking through deadlift plateaus

description.en: The barbell shoulder grip upright row is performed with a shoulder-width grip rather than a narrow or wide grip. The medium grip provides a balance between shoulder and trap involvement, hitting the lateral delts and upper traps without the extreme internal shoulder rotation of narrow grip upright rows.

en: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a barbell at thigh level with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back.
Pull the bar up by leading with your elbows, lifting them out to the sides.
Continue pulling until the bar reaches chest level with elbows above the wrists.
Stop before the bar reaches the chin to protect the shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulders and traps at the top.
Lower the bar back down with control.
Balanced shoulder and trap work
Less internal shoulder rotation than narrow grip
Builds shoulder width
Useful for shoulder hypertrophy
Allows progressive loading
Strong upper trap engagement

description.en: The barbell snatch balance is an Olympic lifting drill where you start with the bar on your back, dip slightly, then drop under the bar into a full overhead squat — catching it with arms locked out overhead. It teaches the speed and timing needed to receive the snatch.

en: Place a light barbell across your upper traps with a wide snatch-width grip.
Stand with feet at your pulling width (hip-width).
Dip slightly by bending your knees.
Drive the bar up slightly while simultaneously dropping your body down into a full overhead squat.
Catch the bar overhead with arms locked out in the bottom of the overhead squat.
Your feet should jump to your receiving width (shoulder-width or slightly wider) as you drop.
Stand up from the overhead squat with the bar locked out.
Use light weight. This is a speed and timing drill.
Teaches snatch receiving speed and timing
Builds overhead squat stability
Develops confidence dropping under the bar
Essential Olympic lifting drill
Improves overhead mobility under load
Builds foot transition timing

description.en: The bottle weighted upright row uses weighted bottles or jugs to load a standing upright row. The bottles travel close to the body up to chest height with the elbows leading the motion. It is a great at-home shoulder builder.

en: Stand tall holding a weighted bottle in each hand at the front of your thighs.
Set your feet at hip-width and brace your core.
Keep the bottles close to your body.
Pull the bottles straight up the front of the body.
Lead with the elbows above the hands.
Stop when the bottles reach chest height.
Pause briefly and squeeze the side delts.
Lower with control to the start.
Builds shoulder width at home
No dumbbells required
Easy to scale loading
Targets side delts and traps
Travel-friendly setup
Strong at-home option

description.en: The cable high triceps extension uses a high cable pulley with rope or bar attachment. By facing away from the cable and bending forward slightly, you extend the cable forward and down for a tricep extension. The angle creates strong stretch on the triceps long head with constant cable tension.

en: Set a cable to the highest pulley with a rope or bar attachment.
Stand facing away from the cable station.
Grip the attachment behind your head with both hands.
Step forward and bend slightly at the hips.
Position your elbows pointing forward and tucked next to your head.
Brace your core.
Extend your elbows to push the attachment forward and away.
Squeeze the triceps at the top, then return to the starting position.
Strong stretch on triceps long head
Constant cable tension through the range
Different angle than tricep pushdowns
Builds tricep size
Useful for hypertrophy training
Strong peak contraction

description.en: The cable seated one arm concentration curl is performed seated on a bench in front of a low cable, with the working elbow braced against the inner thigh. The cable provides constant biceps tension throughout the rep. The braced elbow eliminates cheating and isolates the biceps for a strong peak contraction.

en: Sit on a bench in front of a low cable pulley.
Attach a single D-handle to the cable.
Spread your knees and lean slightly forward.
Hold the handle in one hand with palm up.
Brace the back of your upper arm against the inside of your thigh.
Curl the handle up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top.
Lower the handle slowly to the start. Complete reps on one side before switching.
Strict biceps isolation
Constant cable tension
Eliminates cheating and momentum
Strong peak contraction
Allows unilateral focus
Builds biceps shape

description.en: The cable split stance horizontal pallof press is performed in a split stance with one foot forward, pressing a cable handle straight out from the chest. The split stance challenges hip stability while the press challenges anti-rotation core strength. It is a strong functional core builder.

en: Set a cable to chest height and stand to one side of the machine.
Get into a split stance with one foot forward and one back.
Hold the handle at chest level with both hands.
Brace your core hard against the cable pull.
Press the handle straight out from your chest to full extension.
Resist the cable trying to rotate you toward the machine.
Pause briefly at full extension.
Bring the handle slowly back to your chest. Complete reps before switching stances.
Trains anti-rotation core
Challenges hip stability
Builds functional core strength
Useful for athletes
Improves trunk stability
Carries over to lifts and sports

description.en: The dumbbell front plank arm leg raise holds a high plank position with a light dumbbell in one hand. From the plank, you alternate raising the dumbbell forward while extending the opposite leg back. The contralateral pattern challenges anti-rotation and total body stability.

en: Get into a high plank position with a light dumbbell in your right hand.
Position your hands shoulder-width apart, body in a straight line.
Set your feet hip-width apart for stability.
Brace your core hard and squeeze your glutes.
Raise the right arm forward while extending the left leg back.
Bring both to shoulder and hip height respectively.
Hold for one count.
Lower the arm and leg back to the plank position. Switch sides each rep.
Strong anti-rotation core challenge
Builds total body stability
Develops contralateral coordination
Strong glute and shoulder engagement
Loaded variation of bird dog plank
Useful for core stability programs

description.en: The dumbbell high curl is a bicep curl performed with your elbows elevated to shoulder height, curling the dumbbells toward your head. The elevated arm position provides a unique stimulus and a strong peak contraction at the top. It mimics the front double-bicep pose in bodybuilding and is an effective finishing exercise.

en: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand. Raise your elbows out to the sides at shoulder height, upper arms parallel to the floor.
Your forearms should point forward with palms facing up. Brace your core.
Curl both dumbbells toward your head by bending at the elbows. Keep your upper arms at shoulder height.
Continue until your hands are near your ears. Squeeze your biceps hard at the top.
Lower the dumbbells under control back to the starting position with forearms pointing forward.
Keep your elbows elevated throughout — do not let them drop.
Use light weight. This is a finishing exercise focused on contraction quality.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Unique bicep contraction from the elevated arm position
Strong peak contraction mimicking the double-bicep pose
Excellent finisher for bicep workouts
Builds the bicep peak
Works at home with light dumbbells
Trains shoulder endurance as a secondary benefit

description.en: The dumbbell rear lunge front raise combines two movements into one efficient combo. As you step back into a reverse lunge, you raise the dumbbells forward to shoulder height. The move trains the legs through the lunge and the front delts through the raise simultaneously.

en: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your body.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back.
Step back with your right leg into a reverse lunge.
Lower until your back knee approaches the floor.
As you reach the bottom of the lunge, raise both dumbbells forward to shoulder height.
Pause briefly with the lunge depth and arms raised.
Lower the dumbbells back down as you drive through the front foot to stand.
Repeat on the other leg, alternating sides each rep.
Trains legs and shoulders together
Builds front delt strength
Single-leg work corrects imbalances
Strong cardiovascular component
Time-efficient compound combo
Improves coordination across movement patterns

description.en: The dumbbell Romanian deadlift (RDL) is a hip-hinge exercise performed with a dumbbell in each hand. Unlike a conventional deadlift, the RDL starts standing with the weights at the hips and lowers them with a soft, fixed knee bend. It places the hamstrings under deep load through a long stretch, making it the gold-standard accessory for building hamstring and glute size.

en: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with palms facing your body.
Set a soft, fixed bend in your knees and lock that angle in. The knees should not change angle during the lift.
Pull your shoulders back, lift your chest tall, and brace your core hard.
Begin the descent by pushing your hips straight back. Let the dumbbells slide down the front of your legs.
Keep the dumbbells in light contact with your legs the entire way down. Maintain a flat back.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings — typically when the dumbbells reach mid-shin or just below your knees.
Reverse the movement by driving your hips forward to stand back up. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
Stand fully tall but do not lean back. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Builds the hamstrings through a long, loaded stretch
Heavily targets the glutes through hip extension
Easier on the lower back than the conventional deadlift
Excellent accessory for the deadlift and squat
Improves hamstring flexibility through loaded stretching
Works at home with a single pair of dumbbells

description.en: The dumbbell seated tuck twisting crunch on floor combines a knee tuck with a twisting crunch. The lifter sits balanced on the tailbone holding a dumbbell, twists side to side, and tucks the knees in toward the chest. The combo hammers the abs and obliques.

en: Sit on the floor balanced on the tailbone with knees bent.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands at chest height.
Lean back slightly and lift the feet off the floor.
Brace your core hard.
Twist the torso to bring the dumbbell to one side.
As you twist tuck the knees in toward the chest.
Twist back through center extending the legs out.
Twist to the other side and tuck the knees again.
Strong oblique builder
Trains rotational core
Builds the abs
Useful core finisher
Strong dumbbell move
Builds full ab strength

description.en: The dumbbell single-leg split squat is a stationary split squat holding dumbbells at the sides. You stand in a fixed split stance and lower and rise without stepping. It is essentially the same as the dumbbell static lunge under a different name.

en: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Step one foot forward into a split stance. Fix this position for the set.
Lower your back knee toward the floor by bending both knees.
Descend until your back knee is just above the floor.
Drive through your front foot to rise.
Complete reps, then switch sides.
Keep torso upright throughout.
Use moderate weight. Aim for 10 to 12 reps per leg.
Focused loading on the front leg
No stepping or balance challenge
Builds quad and glute strength unilaterally
Easy to load progressively
Exposes left-right imbalances
Simple setup

description.en: The lever hack squat is performed on a 45-degree hack squat machine where you stand on a platform with your back against a sliding pad. The machine path lets you focus heavily on the quads with full back support. It allows heavy loading with no balance demands and is one of the best machine quad builders.

en: Step onto the platform of the hack squat machine.
Position your back against the sliding pad with shoulder pads above your shoulders.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Grip the handles and unrack the safety.
Brace your core and pull your back tight to the pad.
Squat down by bending your knees and pushing your hips back slightly.
Continue until your thighs are parallel to the platform or deeper.
Drive up through your heels to stand back to the starting position. Re-rack the safety.
Heavy quad loading with back support
Eliminates balance demands
Allows progressive heavy weight
Builds quad size and strength
Different stimulus than free squats
Useful for hypertrophy training

description.en: The high bar inverted row is a more upright variation of the inverted row using a high bar. The steeper body angle reduces the load relative to a low bar version. It is an excellent regression for beginners or for higher rep back work.

en: Set a barbell in a power rack at chest height.
Stand under the bar and grip it with hands shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet forward until the body forms a slight diagonal.
Brace your core and squeeze your shoulder blades down.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving the elbows back.
Squeeze the upper back at the top of the row.
Lower with control until the arms are straight again.
Keep the body in a straight line throughout.
Upright body angle is easier
Great inverted row regression
No advanced equipment needed
Builds back and biceps
Easy to scale by foot position
Useful for beginners

description.en: The hip raise bridge II is a glute bridge variation with the arms extended overhead on the floor. The arm position changes the lever and adds latissimus engagement. It is a useful glute bridge variation for trainees who want to combine back and hip work.

en: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Extend the arms overhead on the floor with palms up.
Set the feet hip width apart.
Brace your core and squeeze the glutes.
Drive through the heels to lift the hips up.
Extend the hips to a straight line with the body.
Reach the arms long overhead at the top.
Lower the hips back down with control.
Strong glute builder
Trains the lats
No equipment needed
Builds the hamstrings
Useful glute builder
Easy to scale

description.en: The jackknife sit-up (V-up) simultaneously lifts the arms and legs from a flat position to meet in the middle, forming a V shape. It targets both the upper and lower abs through full range of motion in one movement.

en: Lie flat on your back. Arms extended overhead, legs extended.
Simultaneously raise your torso and legs, reaching your hands toward your toes.
Your body forms a V at the top.
Touch or reach toward your toes.
Lower everything back to flat under control.
That is one rep.
Move with control — do not use momentum.
Aim for 10 to 15 reps.
Works upper and lower abs simultaneously
Full range of motion core exercise
No equipment needed
Challenging and effective
Builds ab strength through complete range
Develops coordination

description.en: The kettlebell bottoms up to knee Turkish get up is a half range Turkish get up done with the kettlebell flipped upside down. Stopping at the knee position keeps the focus on shoulder stability and grip while reducing total volume.

en: Lie on the back with one arm extended overhead holding a kettlebell upside down.
Bend the same side knee with the foot flat.
Brace the core and lock the working shoulder.
Roll up onto the opposite forearm then to the opposite hand.
Press through the floor and lift the hips.
Sweep the straight leg under and back to a kneeling position.
Pause at the half kneel with the bell still inverted overhead.
Reverse the steps to return to the start.
Brutal shoulder stability drill.
Builds grip strength.
Trains the core for total body control.
Useful for athletic carryover.
Bottoms up grip is humbling.

description.en: The kettlebell goblet squat is a front-loaded squat performed with a single kettlebell held at chest height by the horns (sides of the handle). The kettlebell version offers a slightly different feel than a dumbbell — the offset weight distribution challenges the upper back and core in a unique way. It is one of the most accessible and useful squat variations for any fitness level.

en: Pick up a kettlebell and grip it by the horns (the two sides of the handle, just below where the handle joins the bell). The bell hangs upside down against your chest.
Hold the kettlebell tight against your sternum with elbows pointing straight down.
Set your feet just outside shoulder-width with toes slightly turned out.
Brace your core, take a deep breath, and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Sit your hips down and back, pushing your knees out toward your toes as you descend.
Squat until your elbows touch the inside of your knees or your hip crease drops below the top of your knee.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then drive through your full foot to stand back up.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, reset your breath, and repeat.
Teaches proper squat mechanics with a built-in front-loaded counterweight
Builds quads, glutes, hamstrings, and core in one movement
Trains shoulder, upper-back, and grip endurance through the loaded hold
Encourages a deep, upright squat naturally
Highly portable — only needs one kettlebell and a small space
Excellent warm-up before heavier squat work

description.en: The kettlebell one-arm floor press is a pressing exercise performed lying on the floor with a single kettlebell. The floor limits the range of motion, reducing shoulder stress while allowing heavy single-arm pressing. The unilateral loading builds core anti-rotation strength.

en: Lie on the floor with a KB next to your right side. Roll to grip it and bring it to your right shoulder.
Lie flat on your back. Bend your right knee with foot flat for stability. Left leg extended.
Hold the KB at your right shoulder in the rack position.
Press the KB straight up to lockout.
Lower under control until your right elbow touches the floor.
Pause briefly on the floor. Press back up.
Complete reps, then switch sides.
The floor stops the elbow — no over-stretching the shoulder.
Floor limits range for shoulder safety
Builds pressing strength unilaterally
Core anti-rotation from single-arm loading
No bench needed
Easy to set up
Excellent at-home pressing exercise

description.en: The kettlebell pullover 3 month position is a pullover performed in the FRC 3 month position. The lifter lies on the back with knees bent at 90 degrees over the hips and lower back pressed flat. The lifter performs a pullover from this position to bias core stability.

en: Lie on your back on the floor.
Bend the knees and lift the feet so the knees are over the hips at 90 degrees.
Press the lower back firmly into the floor.
Hold a kettlebell in both hands with arms extended over the chest.
Brace your core and keep the lower back pressed.
Lower the kettlebell back behind the head with arms slightly bent.
Stop when the upper arms reach near the floor.
Pull the kettlebell back over the chest using the lats.
Trains core stability
Strong lat builder
Useful FRC mobility move
Builds core strength
Strong kettlebell move
Useful for athletes

description.en: The kick side jump is a plyometric exercise where you hop laterally to one side and kick the opposite leg out to the side at the peak of the hop. It builds lateral power, hip mobility, and core engagement while providing intense cardiovascular conditioning.

en: Stand on your left foot with right foot slightly off the floor.
Hop to the right, landing on your right foot.
As you land on the right, kick your left leg out to the left side at hip height.
Quickly return your left foot to the ground next to your right.
Hop to the left now, landing on your left foot.
Kick your right leg out to the right side at hip height.
Continue alternating side hops with side kicks.
Move with rhythm and control. Perform for 20 to 45 seconds per set.
Builds lateral power and hip mobility
Develops core engagement and balance
Excellent cardiovascular conditioning
Trains coordination and rhythm
No equipment needed
Engaging plyometric variation

description.en: The knee-to-chest stretch is a gentle lower-back and glute stretch performed lying on your back, pulling one or both knees toward your chest. It decompresses the lumbar spine, stretches the glutes and hamstrings, and relieves lower-back tension. It is one of the simplest and most effective stretches for back health.

en: Lie flat on your back with both legs extended.
Bend your right knee and bring it toward your chest. Clasp both hands around your right shin or behind your right thigh.
Gently pull your right knee closer to your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch in your right glute and lower back.
Keep your left leg flat on the floor (or bend the left knee with foot flat for less intensity).
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch.
Release and switch to the left knee.
For a deeper stretch, pull both knees to your chest simultaneously and rock gently side to side.
Perform two to three holds per side.
Relieves lower-back tension and tightness
Stretches the glutes and hip extensors
Decompresses the lumbar spine
Gentle enough for daily use and rehabilitation
No equipment needed
Calming and restorative

description.en: The lying leg raise and hold combines a leg raise with a static top hold. The pause at the top adds isometric tension and builds endurance in the lower abs and hip flexors.

en: Lie flat on your back with the legs extended.
Place the hands at your sides for support.
Brace the core and press the lower back to the floor.
Keeping the legs straight, lift them up toward the ceiling.
Stop when the legs are roughly vertical.
Hold the top position for several seconds while squeezing the abs.
Lower the legs back down with control to just above the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Builds isometric core strength at the top of the leg raise.
Hammers the lower abs and hip flexors.
No equipment needed.
Trains anterior core endurance.
Improves mind muscle connection.
Carryover to L sit and front lever progressions.

description.en: The resistance band jump squat adds resistance band tension to a plyometric squat jump. Standing on the band with the loops around your shoulders or held at chest level, the band stretches as you jump, increasing the load through the concentric. The combination builds explosive lower body power with progressive resistance.

en: Stand on a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart.
Loop the band over your shoulders or hold the ends at chest level.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back.
Squat down by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Drive up explosively, jumping off the floor against the band tension.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees bent.
Immediately lower into the next squat.
Continue jumping for the duration of the set.
Adds resistance to plyometric jumps
Builds explosive lower body power
Strong cardiovascular component
Develops landing mechanics under load
Useful for athletic conditioning
Easy to scale by changing band tension

description.en: The resistance band lateral walk is a glute activation drill where you place a band around your thighs or ankles and step laterally while maintaining tension. The lateral direction maximizes gluteus medius activation, making it one of the best drills for hip stability, knee tracking, and overall lower-body warm-up.

en: Place a mini band around your thighs (above the knees) or around your ankles for more difficulty.
Stand in a quarter-squat — hips back, knees bent, feet hip-width apart.
Push your knees outward to load the band.
Step your right foot to the right 6 to 12 inches. Maintain band tension.
Step your left foot to the right to follow, keeping the same hip-width stance.
Continue stepping to the right for the desired distance (10 to 20 steps).
Step back to the left for the same distance.
Keep your hips level and your knees pushed out throughout.
Maximally activates the gluteus medius
Excellent warm-up for squats, deadlifts, and lunges
Improves knee tracking and hip stability
Helps prevent knee valgus
Highly portable
Easy to scale with different band thicknesses

description.en: The resistance band seated shoulder press performs an overhead press while seated on a chair with a resistance band under your seat or feet. The seated position removes leg drive, isolating the shoulders. It is a strict at-home shoulder press with constant band tension.

en: Sit on a chair. Loop the band under the chair seat or under your feet.
Hold both ends at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Sit tall. Brace your core.
Press both ends overhead by extending your elbows.
Lock out at the top.
Lower under control back to shoulder height.
No leg drive is possible — pure shoulder pressing.
Use a thicker band for more resistance.
Strict shoulder pressing without leg drive
Constant band tension throughout
Portable at-home shoulder exercise
Easy to scale by band thickness
Seated position isolates the shoulders
Joint-friendly

description.en: Reverse Warrior Pose (Viparita Virabhadrasana) is a standing yoga pose performed from a Warrior II stance. You reach the front arm up and overhead while the back hand slides down the back leg, creating a deep lateral stretch through the side body. It opens the intercostals, obliques, and hip flexors.

en: Start in Warrior II: front knee bent, back leg straight, arms extended to the sides, hips open.
Flip your front palm to face the ceiling. Let your back hand slide down your back thigh or calf.
Inhale and reach your front arm up and overhead, arching gently to the back.
Feel the stretch through the front side of your body — ribs, obliques, and hip flexor.
Keep your front knee bent at 90 degrees. Do not let it straighten.
Gaze up toward your extended hand or forward if that strains your neck.
Hold for 5 to 8 breaths. Breathe into the stretched side.
Return to Warrior II, then switch sides.
Deep lateral stretch through the ribs and obliques
Opens the hip flexors and intercostals
Builds leg endurance through the Warrior stance
Improves lateral spinal flexibility
Energizing and expansive pose
Natural transition from Warrior II

description.en: The rocket jump is a vertical plyometric exercise where you start in a quarter-squat with arms back, then explosively jump straight up while reaching both arms overhead — like a rocket launching. It builds vertical jump power, explosive triple extension, and full-body coordination.

en: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Sit your hips back into a quarter-squat with arms reaching back behind you.
Explode upward by extending your hips, knees, and ankles all at once (triple extension).
Swing your arms forward and up overhead as you jump.
Reach as high as possible at the peak of the jump. Fully extend your body.
Land softly with bent knees to absorb the impact. Bring arms back down to load.
Immediately reset and explode into the next rep.
Focus on jumping as high as possible — this is a max-effort exercise.
Perform 3 to 8 reps per set with full recovery between sets.
Builds maximum vertical jump power
Trains explosive triple extension
Develops full-body coordination
Carries over to all jumping sports
No equipment needed
Excellent power-development exercise

description.en: The roll ball lower back is a self myofascial release drill for the lower back. Using a small ball next to the spine rather than directly on it releases the deep paraspinal muscles without pressing on the bones.

en: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat.
Place a massage ball next to the spine in the lower back.
Brace the core and keep the head supported.
Press the lower back gently into the ball.
Roll slowly side to side along the muscle.
Pause on tender spots for several breaths.
Avoid pressing the ball directly onto the spine.
Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Releases the lower back muscles.
Improves spinal mobility.
Reduces lumbar tightness.
Useful after heavy lifting.
Joint friendly release.

description.en: The roll ball pectoral release is a self myofascial release drill for the chest. Pressing a ball into the pec against a wall releases knots from heavy pressing work and prolonged sitting.

en: Stand facing a wall with a massage ball in one hand.
Place the ball against the chest near the shoulder.
Press the body into the wall with the ball trapped between.
Brace the core and stay tall.
Roll the chest slowly over the ball.
Pause on tender spots for several breaths.
Cover the upper inner and outer chest.
Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Releases the chest.
Improves shoulder posture.
Reduces front body tightness.
Useful after pressing work.
Joint friendly release.

description.en: The lever seated hip abduction is performed on a dedicated hip abduction machine where you sit with pads against your outer thighs and push your legs apart against machine resistance. It isolates the gluteus medius and tensor fasciae latae — critical muscles for hip stability and knee health.

en: Sit in the hip abduction machine with your back against the pad.
Place the outside of your thighs against the pads. Grip the handles.
Start with legs together (or slightly apart).
Push your legs apart against the machine resistance.
Continue until your legs are fully spread to the machine’s range.
Squeeze your outer glutes at the fully open position. Hold briefly.
Slowly bring your legs back together under control.
Do not let the weight stack rest between reps. Aim for 15 to 20 reps per set.
Isolates the gluteus medius and tensor fasciae latae
Easy to load progressively
Improves hip stability and knee tracking
Simple execution
Comfortable seated position
Useful for glute development and rehab

description.en: The seated hip external rotation is a hip stretch done seated in a chair or on a bench. The mover crosses one ankle over the opposite knee and presses the top knee down. It is a useful figure four stretch for the glutes.

en: Sit on a chair or bench with the back tall.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Place the hand of the lifted leg on its knee.
Brace your core and keep the chest up.
Press the lifted knee gently down toward the floor.
Lean forward at the hips for a deeper stretch.
Hold the stretch in the glute and hip.
Release with control. Finish then switch sides.
Stretches the glutes
Mobilizes the hips
Strong figure four stretch
Useful for desk workers
Builds hip range

description.en: Shoulder circles are a simple mobility drill where you rotate your arms in large circles forward and backward. They warm up the shoulder joint through its full range of motion, mobilize the rotator cuff, and improve shoulder flexibility. They are one of the simplest pre-workout shoulder warm-ups available.

en: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Extend both arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
Begin making small forward circles with your arms. Each rep, increase the size of the circles.
Continue circling forward for 10 reps, building from small to large circles.
Reverse direction and circle backward for 10 reps.
Keep your arms straight throughout. Move from the shoulder joint, not the elbows.
Maintain good posture — chest up, core braced.
Perform 1 to 2 sets of 10 reps each direction as a warm-up.
Move slowly and with control — this is a mobility drill, not a momentum exercise.
Warms up the shoulder joint through full range of motion
Mobilizes the rotator cuff
Improves shoulder flexibility
Excellent pre-workout shoulder warm-up
No equipment needed
Quick and easy — takes less than a minute

description.en: The side plank II is a variation of the standard side plank with a slightly modified setup, often involving a different leg or arm position. The hold builds isometric oblique strength and shoulder stability. It is a strong choice for varied core training.

en: Lie on your right side with legs stacked.
Prop yourself up on your right forearm with elbow under shoulder.
Position your feet stacked or staggered.
Place your left hand on your hip or extend it overhead.
Brace your core hard.
Lift your hips off the floor into a side plank position.
Hold a straight line from head to heels.
Hold for the duration. Lower hips down with control. Switch sides.
Builds isometric oblique strength
Strong shoulder stability work
No equipment required
Develops anti-lateral flexion strength
Easy to scale by adjusting time
Useful for core training

description.en: The split jump to box is a plyometric drill that pairs an explosive split jump with a box landing. The move develops single leg power, lateral hip drive, and reactive strength for athletes.

en: Stand in a split stance facing a sturdy plyo box.
Lower into a deep lunge with the back knee close to the floor.
Drive explosively up off the front foot and back foot together.
Switch the legs in midair so the opposite foot lands forward on the box.
Land softly on the box with the front foot.
Tap the back foot lightly behind on the box.
Step back down to the floor and reset into the split stance.
Continue alternating sides for all reps.
Builds explosive single leg power.
Trains landing mechanics on a raised surface.
Develops athletic reactive strength.
Improves coordination and air time control.
Spikes heart rate for cardio benefit.
Carryover to sprinting and jumping sports.

description.en: Stair up is the basic drill of climbing stairs at a steady pace. Whether using a staircase, stadium steps, or a stair machine, the continuous step-up motion builds leg endurance and elevates the heart rate. It is a strong choice for low-equipment cardio that also strengthens the legs.

en: Position yourself at the bottom of a flight of stairs.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back.
Step up onto the first stair with your right foot.
Drive through the right heel to lift your body up.
Bring the left foot up to the next stair.
Continue climbing one stair at a time at a steady pace.
Maintain a steady rhythm with your arms swinging naturally.
Builds leg endurance
Elevates heart rate
Strong glute and quad work
Easy on the joints
No equipment beyond stairs needed
Useful for cardio circuits

description.en: The stalder press is an advanced gymnastics skill where you press from a seated straddle position (legs wide, hips between your hands) up to a handstand without jumping. It demands extreme hamstring flexibility, hip compression strength, and overhead pressing power. It is a staple skill in artistic gymnastics.

en: Start seated on the floor in a wide straddle with hands on the floor between your legs.
Lean forward onto your hands, shifting your weight onto your palms.
Using hip flexor and shoulder strength, lift your hips up while keeping your legs in a straddle.
Continue pressing upward, stacking your hips over your shoulders.
As your hips rise above your hands, begin closing your legs together overhead.
Press all the way up to a full handstand.
This requires elite flexibility, compression, and pressing strength.
Train with parallettes for extra clearance and handstand press progressions.
Builds elite pressing and compression strength
Demands extreme hamstring flexibility
Foundational gymnastics skill
Develops body control and balance
Impressive calisthenics achievement
No equipment needed (parallettes help)

description.en: The standing hamstrings and back stretch is a standing forward fold. Folding from the hips with relaxed knees lets the spine hang heavy and stretches the hamstrings and lower back.

en: Stand with the feet hip width apart.
Place the hands on the hips.
Inhale to lengthen the spine.
Exhale and fold forward from the hips.
Allow the arms and head to hang down.
Soften the knees if the hamstrings are tight.
Reach the hands toward the floor or shins.
Hold the stretch for the desired duration.
Stretches the hamstrings and lower back.
Lengthens the calves through the heel position.
No equipment needed.
Calms the mind in classical yoga practice.
Improves dynamic flexibility.
Excellent warm up before lower body training.

description.en: The strongman crucifix hold is an isometric endurance event where you hold weights extended out to the sides at shoulder height (like a crucifix) for maximum duration. It builds extreme lateral deltoid and shoulder endurance. Even light weights become brutally difficult within 30 seconds.

en: Stand tall. Hold a dumbbell or weight in each hand.
Raise both arms out to the sides at shoulder height — forming a T or crucifix position.
Keep arms straight and at shoulder height.
Hold for as long as possible.
The event ends when you can no longer hold the weights at shoulder height.
Breathe steadily. Focus on maintaining the position.
Even 10 to 25 lb dumbbells are extremely challenging for extended holds.
Build up hold times progressively.
Builds extreme lateral deltoid endurance
Tests mental toughness
Strongman competition event
Simple setup
Even light weights are challenging
Develops shoulder stability

description.en: The suspender abduction lunge uses suspension straps as a balance aid during a lateral abduction lunge. The straps allow you to lower deeper into the lunge by sharing some bodyweight. The lateral lunge pattern emphasizes the glutes, adductors, and inner thighs.

en: Adjust suspension straps to mid-length and grip the handles.
Stand facing the anchor point with feet hip-width apart.
Step out to the side with your right leg into a lateral lunge.
Bend the right knee and push your hips back.
Keep the left leg extended out to the side.
Lower as deep as your mobility allows, using the straps for support.
Push through the right foot to drive back to standing.
Repeat for desired reps, then switch sides.
Suspension straps allow deeper lunges
Trains the glutes and inner thighs
Builds lateral stability
Develops single-leg strength
Improves hip mobility
Accessible for newer lifters

description.en: The suspender mountain climber push up combines a TRX push up with mountain climbers. The lifter places the feet in TRX cradles and performs a push up, then drives the knees in alternating mountain climbers. The combo trains the chest, core, and cardio.

en: Set the suspension trainer foot cradles low.
Place both feet in the cradles facing down.
Set the hands on the floor in a high plank position.
Brace your core and keep the body in a straight line.
Perform a push up lowering and pressing back up.
At the top drive one knee toward the chest.
Switch and drive the other knee toward the chest.
Continue alternating mountain climbers then another push up.
Brutal full body combo
Trains the chest and core
Adds cardio to push ups
Strong TRX move
Useful conditioning combo
Builds the core

description.en: Tree Pose (Vrksasana) is a foundational standing balance yoga pose where you stand on one leg with the sole of the opposite foot pressed against the inner thigh, calf, or ankle of the standing leg. It builds single-leg balance, ankle stability, hip mobility, and concentration.

en: Stand tall in Mountain Pose. Shift your weight onto your left foot.
Bend your right knee and place the sole of your right foot against the inside of your left thigh, calf, or ankle. Avoid placing it directly on the knee joint.
Press your right foot into your left leg and your left leg back into your right foot — the equal pressure helps with stability.
Bring your hands together at your heart center in prayer position. For more challenge, extend arms overhead.
Find a fixed point to gaze at for balance. Breathe deeply.
Square your hips forward. Engage your standing-leg glute for stability.
Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply and stay focused.
Lower your right foot and switch sides. Use a wall for support if needed.
Builds single-leg balance and ankle stability
Strengthens the standing-leg glute and core
Improves hip mobility and external rotation
Develops focus and concentration
Foundational yoga balance pose
No equipment needed

description.en: The weighted overhead press step up is a full-body combo where the lifter steps up onto a box with dumbbells and presses them overhead at the top. The combination builds legs and shoulders together for a strong functional move.

en: Stand in front of a sturdy box with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level.
Set your feet at hip-width and brace your core.
Place one foot flat on the box.
Drive through the front heel to step up onto the box.
As you reach the top, press the dumbbells straight overhead.
Lock out the arms at the top.
Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder level.
Step back down with control. Alternate legs each rep.
Trains legs and shoulders together
Combo move saves time
Builds full-body strength
Strong conditioning effect
Useful for athletes
Excellent functional move

description.en: Wrist circles are a simple mobility drill where you rotate your wrists in circular motions to mobilize the wrist joints. They warm up the wrists, improve mobility, and are essential before any push-up, plank, or pressing work. They are particularly important for lifters with grip-intensive training.

en: Stand or sit. Extend both arms forward at shoulder height.
Make a loose fist with each hand.
Begin rotating your fists in clockwise circles. Move only at the wrist.
Make 10 to 15 large circles.
Reverse direction and circle counterclockwise for the same number of reps.
For deeper mobility: open your hands and spread fingers wide between sets.
Move slowly through the full range of motion.
Perform 1 to 2 sets as part of an upper-body warm-up.
Improves wrist mobility
Warms up the wrist joint
Essential before push-ups or planks
Quick and accessible
No equipment needed
Useful for desk workers
